sentences.text: Collinsella was created when Eubacterium aerofaciens, isolated in large numbers from human faeces, was transferred to the new genus as Collinsella aerofaciens.
Strains of this group are separated by their fermentation of sugars such as sucrose, cellobiose, aesculin, salicin and amygdalin.
Collinsella aerofaciens is an actinomycete that appears prominently in human gut microbiome association studies.
A study reported that low dietary fibre intake raised Collinsella abundance in overweight and obese pregnant women, with genus abundance positively correlated with circulating insulin.

Studies have reported higher Collinsella abundance in biopsy-proven non-alcoholic steatohepatitis, and the genus usually correlates with pro-inflammatory responses, with favourable cancer immunotherapy response a noted exception.
